events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWPHI

The National Weather Service in Mount Holly NJ has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Lower Delaware Bay...
Coastal waters from Great Egg Inlet NJ to Fenwick Island DE out 20
nm...
Outer waters from Cape May NJ to Fenwick Island DE from 20 to 60
nm...

* Until 445 PM EDT.

* At 343 PM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located over Rehoboth
Beach, moving east at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Overfalls Shoal, Five Fathoms Buoy, Buoy 4fb, Buoy 3fb, Cape May
Reef, Cape Henlopen, Rehoboth Beach, Buoy 2ms, Wildwood Reef, and
Indian River Inlet Bridge.

events.summary:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Wayne County in southern Utah...

* Until 445 PM MDT.

* At 140 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.25 and 0.75 inches of
rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Capitol Reef National Park and Fruita.

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Garfield County in southern Utah...

* Until 445 PM MDT.

* At 139 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Muley Twist and Burr Trail area of Capitol
Reef National Park. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Muley Twist Canyons and the Burr Trail in Capitol Reef National
Park.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Moody Creek, North Fork Silver Falls Creek, Bullfrog Creek, Muley
Creek and Halls Creek.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...South Central Gallatin County in south central Montana...
Southeastern Madison County in southwestern Montana...

* WHEN...Until 445 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 137 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain with rainfall
rates in excess of 1 inch per hour due to thunderstorms. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory
area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Yellowstone Village.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 338 PM EDT, a confirmed tornado was located over Norridgewock, or
near Skowhegan, moving northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Damaging tornado.

SOURCE...Weather spotters confirmed tornado.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

This tornado will be near...
Skowhegan, Madison, and Norridgewock around 345 PM EDT.

Other locations impacted by this tornadic thunderstorm include
Cornville, Athens, Canaan, and Hartland.

events.summary:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar in...
East Central Custer County in southeastern Colorado...
Southwestern Pueblo County in southeastern Colorado...

* Until 430 PM MDT.

* At 125 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar. The expected
rainfall rate is 0.3 to 0.8 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the
burn scar will result in debris flow. The debris flow can consist
of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Middle Aspen Acres Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Beulah.

This includes the following high risk locations...
Beulah Water Intake and Northcreek Road from Red Mountain Camp to
Beulah.
